situations: It is dark in your room and you want to read. You press a switch on the small thing on your desk and it gives light.
In a furniture shop you look for something that hangs from the ceiling or stands on the floor and has a bulb inside.
Your friend visits and says it is too dark. You turn on the light on the table next to your bed. Which word means 'lamp'?
At night you sleep and see strange pictures in your head, for example you are flying over the sea.
In class you look out of the window and imagine a holiday on a beach far away instead of listening.
In the morning you tell your friend what happened in your head while you slept: you could fly! Which verb means 'to dream'?
On the kitchen wall hangs a big sheet with all the days of the month. You write the dentist's appointment on it.
It is December and in a shop you buy a poster with twelve months for the new year.
You check on your phone which weekday the 15th is and add a meeting. Which word means 'calendar'?
It is 3 a.m. and you cannot sleep. You lie in bed with your eyes open.
After a strong coffee in the morning you are no longer sleepy and your mind is clear.
Your baby sister was sleeping, but now her eyes are open and she looks around. Which word means 'awake'?
The waiter offers you more rice, but your plate is already full. You say: 'No more, thanks, I have had ... '.
At the till you count your money: you need 10 euros and you have 12. You have all you need.
Your mother pours milk into your glass and you say stop when there is the right amount. Which word means 'enough'?
You come into the kitchen and sit down at the table, on a piece of furniture with four legs and a back, but no arms.
At a party there are not enough seats for everyone, so someone brings one more from the other room.
After class the teacher asks you to push this seat under the desk before you leave. Which word means 'chair'?
You live next to a busy road. On holiday in a mountain village you hear no cars and no voices, only birds.
Your neighbours are shouting in the hallway. You open the door and ask them politely for some quiet.
After a very hard week you lie on the sofa and do nothing at all. You feel calm and relaxed. What do you need now?

en: to carry, to wear, to bear
situations: It is cold outside, so you have a thick jacket and a scarf on your body.
Your neighbour has many heavy shopping bags. You help her bring them up the stairs in your hands.
A porter takes your suitcase from the train to the taxi, holding its weight. Which verb means 'to carry'?
A friend asks you for the capital of Mongolia and you know nothing at all. You shrug and say you have not got a clue.
You feel that something is wrong, but you cannot prove it. It is only a vague suspicion.
Your teacher asks if you know how the machine works. You shake your head: you do not have the faintest notion about it.
A film about deep-sea animals keeps you watching for two hours without looking at your phone.
Your classmate tells you a story about his trip that makes you want to hear more.
The book is not boring at all. Which word means 'interesting'?
Your friend sends you a message with a blue underlined text. You tap it and a web page opens.
You want to share a funny video. You copy the web address and paste it into the chat.
An email says: 'Click on this to reset your password.' What do you click on?
Tomorrow you fly to Berlin. Tonight you put your clothes and shoes into the suitcase.
It is your friend's birthday. You cover the gift in colourful paper and tie a ribbon around it.
You buy a cake and the seller puts it in a box for you. Which verb means 'to pack'?
On Sunday you go to a museum hall to look at paintings by a famous artist that are shown for two months.
Your class visits a place where cars from the 1950s are displayed for visitors to look at.
Your friend invites you to see her photos hanging on the walls of a small gallery. Which word means 'exhibition'?
You go swimming every week on the second day of the working week, never on another day. Which adverb says this happens regularly on that day?
A sign at the market says that the stalls are open every week on the day after Monday, but not on the other days.
The bakery has its day off every week on the day between Monday and Wednesday. Which adverb means 'on Tuesdays'?
You always read about planets and watch videos about space because it fascinates you. This curiosity about a topic is what?
In a job interview you are asked about your hobbies. You say you have a strong ... in photography.
A salesman shows you an expensive watch. You shake your head: you feel no wish to know more or to buy it.
You play football in the rain and come home with mud all over your trousers.
The kitchen window has not been washed for a year and you can hardly see through it.
Your hands are black after fixing your bike chain. Which word means 'dirty'?

en: to quarrel, to argue, to dispute
situations: Two brothers shout at each other because both want the last piece of pizza.
At work two colleagues have different opinions and speak loudly and angrily about who made the mistake.
Your parents raise their voices about money in the kitchen. Which verb means 'to quarrel'?
At six in the morning a man in a white apron takes fresh bread out of a hot oven. What is his job?
Every morning you go to a small shop on the corner to buy rolls and bread.
Your neighbour asks where you are going. You are heading to the place where bread is made and sold.
Every summer you camp for three days in a field and listen to many bands on big stages.
Your town has an open-air music weekend with food trucks, tents and thousands of young people.
A big event takes place in your city where new movies from many countries are shown over one week. Which word means 'festival'?

en: ground floor, ground level, first floor
situations: You live in a building with four floors. Your friend lives on the level at the same height as the street, so he needs no stairs.
In the lift of a hotel you press the button marked 0 and arrive in the entrance hall.
Your grandmother cannot climb stairs, so she looks for a flat on the level at street height. Which word means 'ground floor'?
You spread butter on bread in a very flat layer, almost see-through.
It is winter, but your jacket is made of very light cloth and does not keep you warm.
Your friend has lost weight and now has a very narrow, slim body. Which word means 'thin'?
You look out of the window in December and white flakes are falling from the sky. Everything outside turns white.
The weather forecast says it will be minus three degrees tomorrow and the children are excited because they might build a man from white flakes.
It is minus two degrees and the clouds are heavy and grey. Which verb means 'to snow'?
You stand outside a café with a friend and point through the door. You say: 'Let's go ...!' meaning 'in, into'.
You are outside by the door of the cellar and wave your friend toward the dark room: 'Come on, ...!'
You throw your dirty clothes into the washing machine. Which direction word, meaning 'into', describes this movement away from you?
At a birthday party someone cuts a cake and gives you a slice. What do you get?
At the market the seller asks how much cheese you want. You ask for a small chunk cut from the big block.
You break your chocolate bar into parts and give one to your friend. Which word means 'piece'?
In the evening the whole family sits on the sofa in front of the TV, in the main room of the flat where you relax.
Guests arrive. You take them into the room with the sofa and the coffee table, not into the kitchen.
You show a visitor around your flat: bedroom, kitchen, bathroom, and the largest room for relaxing and meeting guests. Which word means 'living room'?

en: to fall, to drop, to decline
situations: A glass slips from your hand and drops to the floor, where it breaks.
In autumn the leaves leave the tree and come down to the ground.
At night the temperature goes down from 15 to 5 degrees. Which verb describes this downward movement?
You read a novel and look at the name of the woman who wrote it on the cover.
At a book reading in the library, a woman reads aloud from her own new book. Who is she?
Your teacher says: 'The writer of this story is a woman from Vienna.' Which word means 'author (female)'?

en: with a cold, to have a cold
situations: You have a runny nose, you cough and you sneeze, so you stay at home and drink hot tea.
At the doctor's office he says: 'It is nothing serious, just a mild illness with a sore throat. Rest for a few days.'
Your colleague sneezes all day and has a red nose. You say: 'You look like you have a cold.' Which adjective means 'with a cold'?
Your friend asks what is wrong. You say it is a long story about one problem that must be solved: 'It is a difficult ...'
You cannot remember the name of an object on the shelf, so you say 'Give me that ... over there', using a general word for any object.
Your teacher says: 'This is a serious matter and we must talk about it.' Which general word means 'matter' or 'thing'?
You read a letter in a language you do not know, so you write each sentence again in your own language.
At a business meeting a man says every sentence from one language into another so the foreign guests understand.
You use an app on your phone to turn the menu text into your own language. Which verb means 'to translate'?
At the till you take a small leather case out of your pocket that holds coins, notes and cards.
You lose your small case with money and ID on the bus and go to the lost property office.
For her birthday you give your mother a small holder for coins. Which word means 'wallet' or 'purse'?
Your lessons start at eight and finish before lunch. Which word describes this time of the day, 'in the morning'?
A sign on a shop says it is open from 9 until noon and closed after that. Which adverb names this time of the day?
You tell your boss: 'Between nine and twelve every day I have meetings.' Which time adverb do you use for this part of the day?
After school, Lena works three days a week in a bakery and goes to a vocational school for two days, for three years, to learn the job.
To become a nurse you spend years learning at a hospital and a school. What do you call this period of learning a profession?
Your uncle says: 'I want my son to get a proper vocational education before he starts working.'
The label on the juice says: no sugar, no colouring, no artificial flavours added. Everything comes from nature.
In the mountains there is a lake not made by humans; it formed by itself. What kind of lake is it?
Her hair colour is not dyed; it is how it was from birth. Which word means 'natural'?
On holiday you want to take pictures of the beach, so you take out a device with a lens.
In the shopping mall, small devices on the ceiling film everyone for security.
On your phone you open the app to take a selfie. Which word means 'camera'?

en: to (take a) walk, to (go for a) walk, to stroll
situations: After Sunday lunch your family leaves the house to move slowly and calmly through the park, with no hurry.
It is a sunny evening and you go along the river with your dog at a slow pace.
Your grandfather says: 'After dinner I always take a slow, relaxed stroll around the block.' Which verb is that?
The doctor says: 'Eat well, sleep enough and do sports. It is good for your body.' What is she talking about?
You are never ill, you have energy and no pain. You say you are lucky to have good ...
The cigarette box warns you that smoking harms this. Which word means 'health'?
You turn the key in the front door. The metal part in the door holds it shut.
On a school trip you visit a huge old building with towers where a king once lived.
You lose your key and cannot open the door. You call a locksmith to change the part inside the door that the key fits into.
You have dinner by candlelight with your partner, with soft music and a view of the sea.
A small old town with narrow streets, flowers and a river looks like a picture from a postcard.
Your boyfriend gives you roses and writes you a love letter. Which word means 'romantic'?

en: to remove, to get rid of
situations: There is a red wine stain on the tablecloth, and you scrub until the mark is gone.
The child draws on the wall with a pen. Mum says: 'Clean that off right now!'
Your landlord asks you to take the old furniture out of the cellar and get rid of it. Which verb means 'to remove'?
You call your friend, but nobody answers. A voice asks you to leave a message after the beep.
Your email programme shows 253 new messages in the folder that collects everything sent to your address.
Your phone shows a small icon: two new recorded messages are waiting for you. Which word means 'voicemail'?
It is pouring with rain, so the children play on the floor in the house, not in the garden.
The waiter asks if you want to sit in the garden or in the room. It is cold, so you choose the room.
Your friend asks: 'Is Tom in the garden?' You answer: 'No, he is in the house, not outside.' Which adverb means 'inside'?
You want a new job, so you write a letter and send your CV to the company.
The university asks you to send in documents and a form to get a place to study there.
A company receives fifty of these from candidates for one job. Which word means 'application'?
You put your hand on the radiator to find out if it is warm. Your skin gives you the information.
After a long run your legs are tired and your heart beats fast. You tell your friend how your body seems.
The doctor asks: 'How do you ... today?' Which verb means 'to feel'?
Your friend asks if you want to go to the cinema tonight. You say yes because it sounds nice and you have the wish to go.
It is raining and you stay at home because you do not feel like going out at all.
Someone says: 'I fancy a pizza right now.' Which noun means the 'desire' or wish to do something?
You press your fingers into a fresh sponge cake. It gives way and is not hard at all.
Your cat's fur feels very gentle under your hand and not rough.
The pillow is not firm. It is the opposite of hard. Which word means 'soft'?
At work your team plans a new app for six months, with goals, tasks and a deadline.
In school your group researches and prepares a presentation about rivers over several weeks.
Your uncle plans to build a garden house by himself in the summer. Which word means 'project'?
Your school timetable lists maths, history and art. Each of these is what?
In the fridge door there is a little compartment for the butter. What is this small section called?
At the swimming pool you put your things into a small numbered space with a door and take the key. What is that space called?
You come home sweaty from sport and put on different, clean clothes.
You are going to a wedding after work, so you take off your work shirt and put on a suit in the office.
Before swimming you go into a small cabin and put on your swimsuit instead of your normal clothes. Which verb is that?
The streets are empty and dark and most people sleep. Which adverb says this happens regularly 'at night'?
A nurse works in the hospital during the dark hours, from 10 pm to 6 am.
Stars and the moon shine in the sky only at this time of day, when it is dark. Which adverb names it?
In the garden you grow green pods that climb up a stick and have small seeds inside.
Your grandmother soaks small, oval, dried seeds overnight to cook a soup.
In a tin from the supermarket you find baked ones in tomato sauce. Which word means 'bean'?
Your neighbour was married for ten years, but now her marriage has legally ended.
On a form a man ticks the box for a person whose marriage was officially ended by a court.
Your friend's parents no longer live together and a court has ended their marriage. Which word means 'divorced'?
Two cars crash at a crossing. The police and an ambulance arrive.
A child falls off her bike and breaks her arm. Her parents say it was an unlucky event.
Your colleague is not at work because he hurt his leg when he slipped on the ice. Which word means 'accident'?

en: to notice, to note, to remember, to memorise, to realise
situations: You leave the shop and suddenly realise that the cashier gave you too little change.
Your teacher says: 'Try to keep this phone number in your head until tomorrow.'
Your friend left the party early, but you only became aware of it an hour later. Which verb is that?
Every Tuesday evening you go to the sports hall to practise with your football team and the coach.
In the gym you lift weights for an hour three times a week.
The marathon is in two months, so you run five times a week to prepare. Which word means 'workout' or 'practice'?
After a shower you dry your body with a big soft cloth.
At the pool you lay a big cotton cloth on the sunbed.
In a hotel bathroom there is none left, so you ask the reception for another one. Which word means 'towel'?
The diamond in the ring is not a copy or made of glass. It is genuine.
A child sees a picture of a dragon and asks if it exists outside books. You say: 'No, it is not ...'
A man says: 'My ... name is Peter, but everyone calls me Pete.' He means his true name. Which word means 'real'?

en: to show, to demonstrate, to point, to indicate
situations: A tourist asks for the way. You stretch out your arm and use your finger to direct her to the station.
At the end of your holiday you open your laptop and let your parents see the photos.
The teacher draws on the board how the machine works so the students can see it. Which verb means 'to show'?
On a slice of bread you put a yellow, salty slice that is made from milk.
In a cartoon the little mouse is always looking for yellow, holey food made from milk.
At the dairy counter you ask for 200 grams of Gouda. Which word means 'cheese'?
Your choir practises every week on the day before Friday.
The market takes place weekly on the day between Wednesday and Friday.
You tell a colleague that you always work from home on the fourth day of the working week. Which adverb means 'on Thursdays'?
At school you study the old language of the Romans.
A doctor writes the names of illnesses in the ancient language of the Roman Empire.
In the old days you needed to know this dead language to study medicine. Which word means 'Latin'?
You need a quiet place to study and to borrow books for free with a card.
At university you go to a big building with long shelves of books and reading tables to prepare for exams.
Your child wants a novel but you do not want to buy it. Where can you borrow it? Which word means 'library'?
You touch the cooker plate and burn your finger.
In July it is 38 degrees and everyone is sweating at the beach.
You pour boiling water on a teabag and the cup is too ... to drink. Which word means 'hot'?

en: to carry on, to continue, to proceed, to go on
situations: You are tired during a long walk and stop. Your friend says: 'Come on, do not stop now.'
A fire alarm interrupted the lesson. Afterwards the teacher says: 'Let's keep going with the exercise.'
You did half of your homework and want a break, but then decide to carry on. Which verb means 'to continue'?

en: school trip, class trip, class outing
situations: Your teacher takes the whole class by bus to a youth hostel by the sea for a week.
Parents must pay money and sign a form so their children can join a week away with their classmates.
You sleep in a room with five classmates in a hostel. Which word means 'school trip'?
In the classroom the teacher explains fractions, equations and geometry.
You have a test tomorrow with numbers, algebra and calculating angles.
Your sister loves numbers and wants to study this subject at university. Which word means 'maths'?

en: to do handicrafts, to work on, to tinker, to make (with one's hands)
situations: Before Christmas the kids cut paper and glue stars to hang in the window.
Your father spends Sunday in the garage, building things from wood and wire with his hands.
In kindergarten the children make a card with scissors and glue. Which verb means 'to do handicrafts'?
Your friend asked you to wear a green shirt, but you wore a blue one. You chose another colour than expected.
Two twins look alike, but each one thinks about things in a way that does not match the other.
Your boss says the plan failed, so next time you should try another way. Which adverb means 'differently'?
A man paints large pictures and sells them in a gallery. What is he called?
On the street a man plays violin and paints portraits for passers-by.
Your uncle makes sculptures from metal and shows them in exhibitions. Which word means 'artist' (male)?
Your best friend moves to another country tomorrow. You cry and do not feel like talking.
You watch a film where the dog dies and your eyes get wet.
You failed your exam and you feel very down. Which word means 'sad'?
You boil long thin strips of dough in salted water and serve them with tomato sauce.
In a soup, little yellow strings float next to chicken pieces.
You pick one long thin string out of the pot with a fork to test if it is soft. Which word means 'noodle'?

en: to practise, to practice, to exercise
situations: To play the piano well, you play the same song every day for half an hour.
Before the driving test you drive around the car park again and again with the instructor.
Your teacher says: 'Repeat the words many times and you will learn them.' Which verb means 'to practise'?
In school you have a lesson where you paint pictures and draw with coloured pencils.
In a museum you look at paintings, sculptures and old drawings.
Your friend says that music, painting and theatre are all forms of ... Which word means 'art'?
You want to cook lasagne but do not know the amounts, so you look for the list of ingredients and steps in a cookbook.
You have a bad cough and the doctor writes a note so that the pharmacy gives you medicine.
Your grandmother's pancakes are famous and everyone asks her for the secret instructions. Which word means 'recipe'?
Your friend tells an unbelievable story and you ask if it really happened. He says: 'Yes, it is ...'
In a quiz you must say whether each sentence is correct or false: 'Paris is the capital of France.' You tick the right box.
A story is not made up; it is how it really happened. Which word means 'true'?
Your mother's brother comes to visit with a present.
Your father's brother lives in Hamburg and has two sons, your cousins.
At a family party you point to the man who is the brother of one of your parents. Which word means 'uncle'?
In a pan with oil you cook a steak until it is brown on both sides.
On Sunday your mother puts a chicken in the oven for two hours until it is golden.
You heat oil in a pan and put in eggs and potatoes. Which verb means 'to fry'?
From inside the house you point to the garden door and tell the dog: 'Go ...!' meaning 'out'.
At the end of the meeting the boss opens the door and tells the people to leave the room.
You stand on the balcony and throw a ball away from the room. Which direction word means 'out'?
On holiday you take a ferry to a piece of land that is completely surrounded by water.
Robinson was alone on a piece of land in the sea with no other people.
Mallorca is a piece of land in the sea. Which word means 'island'?
A tourist asks how to get to the station and you explain which streets to follow.
A narrow track in the forest leads to a lake. Hikers follow it on foot.
On your way home you take a shortcut. Which word means 'path' or 'way'?
You run 5 km three times a week and can climb stairs without getting out of breath.
Your grandfather is 80 but still rides a bike every day and feels strong and healthy.
After your illness the doctor says you can do sport again because your body is in good shape. Which word means 'fit'?
Tomorrow is your exam. You cannot do anything more, but you wish very much that it goes well.
Your friend is ill. You think and wish that she gets better soon.
It is cloudy, but you want the sun to come out for the picnic. Which verb means 'to hope'?
The train should have arrived at 8:00 but only comes at 8:20. The sign says twenty minutes more than planned.
Your colleague arrives at the meeting fifteen minutes after the start and says sorry.
The announcement at the airport says flight 123 will leave later than planned. Which word means 'delay'?
At the farm a big brown animal with a mane and four legs pulls a cart.
Girls in riding boots sit on large animals in the riding school and jump over bars.
A cowboy in a film rides one through the desert. Which word means 'horse'?
Your friend shows you a documentary about volcanoes. You say it makes you curious and you want to know more: 'It ... me.'
Football does not catch your attention at all, but music does.
Your teacher tells stories to make the class curious about history. Which verb means 'to interest'?
In summer the whole village meets in the main square with music, beer tents and fireworks.
At Christmas the family has a big meal together with presents and singing. This special occasion is what?
Your neighbours invite everyone to a big party in the garden. Which word means 'celebration'?
At the restaurant the waiter asks: 'Together or ...?' Each person pays their own bill.
The couple still like each other but live in two different flats, apart from one another.
You put paper in one bin and plastic in another, so the two kinds of waste are kept apart. Which word means 'separate'?
A friend asks: 'Can you help me move on Saturday?' You answer with a cheerful word meaning 'sure, no problem'.
Someone asks: 'Do you know Berlin?' You lived there for ten years: '... I know it well!'
Someone asks if you like ice cream on a hot day and you say yes, as is obvious. Which adverb means 'of course'?
Before you go to the supermarket you write what you need on a small sheet of paper.
Your flatmate leaves a short message on the fridge saying he went to work.
After paying at the shop the cashier gives you a small printed sheet that shows what you bought. Which word means 'piece of paper' or 'receipt'?
On Saturday morning you buy fresh vegetables from stalls in the town square.
Farmers sell apples and eggs from small stands under umbrellas.
At Christmas you drink hot spiced wine at a place with wooden huts in the town centre. Which word means 'market'?

en: to organize, to organise, to arrange
situations: You plan a surprise party: you book a room, order a cake and invite the guests.
At work you have to make sure that the meeting room, the projector and the coffee are ready.
Your class goes on a trip and the teacher says: 'Who wants to arrange the tickets?' Which verb means 'to organize'?
At a campfire someone plays songs on an instrument with six strings.
A rock musician plays loudly on a stage with an electric one.
You start lessons to learn an instrument with a wooden body, a neck and strings. Which word means 'guitar'?
At the market the vegetables were picked this morning and still look crisp.
You open the window in the morning and the air is cool and clean.
The bread has just come out of the oven and is not old. Which word means 'fresh'?
Children sit on the floor and move pieces on a board, rolling dice.
On Saturday your football team plays against another team and it ends 2:1.
On the phone your little brother plays an electronic one for hours. Which word means 'game'?

en: to exist, to insist, to pass, to consist, to persist
situations: You studied hard for the driving test and got the result you needed. You succeeded.
The teacher asks what water is made of. You say: 'It ... of hydrogen and oxygen.'
The company was founded in 1900 and is still here today. Which verb means 'to exist'?
You come back to your desk and your phone is not there. It has disappeared.
A friend leaves on holiday for two weeks. He is not here, he is gone.
You say to a fly: 'Go ...!' Which adverb means 'away'?
You have a high fever, aching muscles and chills for a week. The doctor says a virus caused it and you must stay in bed.
In autumn the doctor offers a vaccination against a winter virus that makes many people absent from the office.
You feel terrible, with a fever and body aches. Which noun means 'flu'?
In your tea you squeeze a sour yellow fruit.
You make a cold drink with sugar, water and the juice of a sour yellow fruit.
At the market you buy a yellow citrus fruit that is very sour. Which word means 'lemon'?
You mop the floor and wipe the table until there is no dust left.
After washing your hands with soap they look and smell fresh.
The hotel room was spotless, with no stain anywhere. Which word means 'clean'?
Your soup arrives cold. You call the waiter and tell him you are unhappy about it.
Your neighbours play loud music at 2 a.m., so you go to the landlord and say it is not acceptable.
The hotel room was dirty, so you write to the manager to say how unhappy you are. Which verb means 'to complain'?
Your friend lives three flights of stairs above the entrance of a block of flats, and there is no lift.
The department store has five of these stacked on top of each other, and the shoe section is on the second one.
A skyscraper has forty of them. Which word means 'floor' or 'storey' of a building?
Two teams run up and down a hall and throw an orange ball through a hoop with a net.
In sports class players bounce a ball and try to score through a high ring.
Your tall friend plays for a team and wants to be like the American stars. Which word means 'basketball'?
It is snowing. You put on a long warm piece of clothing over your sweater before you leave.
In the restaurant you hand your outer garment to the staff at the cloakroom.
In winter men and women wear a long warm one over their clothes. Which word means 'coat'?
You sit down in a big soft armchair and feel relaxed, with no pain in your back.
Your new shoes do not hurt at all and you could walk all day in them.
The sofa is not hard or narrow; you could sleep on it. Which word means 'comfortable'?

en: to set, to place, to put
situations: A mother lifts her toddler and puts him down onto the chair so that he sits.
In writing, you add a small mark between two parts of a sentence. What do you do with the comma?
At the start of the year you decide on a goal for yourself and put it down on paper.
You waited at the bus stop for forty minutes and now the bus arrives. You sigh with relief.
After years of studying you receive your diploma. You feel relieved after a long wait.
Your friend comes very late. After a long time of waiting you say what? Which adverb means 'at last'?
You go down the stairs to the dark room under the house to fetch a bottle of wine and old boxes.
In your building the bikes and the washing machine are kept in the lowest part, below the ground floor.
During a storm the family goes to the room below the house to be safe. Which word means 'cellar'?
On holiday you lie on the warm sand next to the sea and build a sandcastle.
You swim in the sea and then dry yourself on a towel on the soft sand by the water.
Families with umbrellas and buckets spend summer days here by the sea. Which word means 'beach'?
In your textbook you use a yellow pen to colour the important sentences.
On a map you draw a cross to show where the hotel is.
The teacher asks you to put a tick next to the correct answers. Which verb means 'to mark'?
A tourist asks you: bus, tram, train or bike? What do you call all these ways of getting around the city?
Your town wants fewer cars, so people should use buses, trains and bicycles instead.
You want to get from the airport to the city centre and ask what is the best one: train, taxi or bus. Which word covers all of them?
You see a building made of grey concrete with broken windows, and nobody likes how it looks.
The dress is torn and the colours do not match. Your friend says it looks awful.
In the fairy tale the witch has a crooked nose and warts. Which word means 'ugly'?
At the end of term you get a number from 1 to 6 for your test.
On sheet music each little black dot on the lines shows a tone that you should play.
Your teacher gave you a 2 for your essay. Which word means 'grade' or 'mark'?
The sky is dark and you hear thunder. You say it will rain, though you are not completely sure.
Your friend asks if you will come to the party. You are likely to come but it is not certain.
The weather report gives an eighty percent chance of rain. Which adverb means 'probably'?

en: to divide, to share, to split
situations: You have one big pizza and two people, so you cut it in half and each person takes one part.
You have a big chocolate bar and give some to your friends so everyone has some.
In maths you calculate twelve by three. Which verb means 'to divide'?
A journalist asks a famous actress many questions about her new film for a magazine.
You go to a company, sit with the manager and answer questions about your skills for a job.

en: to think, to mean, to say

Every week on the day before the weekend, your team goes out for lunch together. Which word says 'every Friday'?

After the concert, a crowd waits outside the hotel to see the band. Who are these people?

Your new colleague greets everybody in a friendly way and asks if you need help. What kind of person is he?
The waiter is polite, helpful and cheerful. You tell your friend: 'The waiter is really ...'

en: to talk, to chat, to have a chat, to converse
situations: Two neighbours meet at the bus stop and spend half an hour speaking about the weather and their children. What do they do?

en: then, at that time, at the time, in those days

Every morning at six you put on running shoes and run slowly through the park for half an hour. What do you do?
The doctor says you should move more, so you start to run slowly and steadily three times a week.
After work your colleague changes clothes and goes running calmly along the river. What does she do?

A tourist asks: 'Which is the main city of this country?' You answer with the name of the biggest political city.

Your father has strict rules: no phone at dinner and bed at nine, no discussion. He is quite ...?
The football coach shouts when players are late and makes them run extra laps. What type of coach is he?
You say: 'The shops, restaurants and the old church are all in the middle of the town.' What do you call that part?
The bus line goes into the middle of the city where all the streets meet. Where does it go?
There is a sign for a place with many offices at the heart of the city. Which word fits?
You send an email: 'Yes, I will come to the meeting on Monday.' What are you doing with the appointment?
The hotel writes to you: 'We say yes, your booking for two nights is correct.' What does the hotel do?
The doctor's assistant calls to say your appointment is definitely on for Thursday. What is she doing?
It is cold in autumn, so you put on a warm woollen top without buttons over your shirt. What is it?

The shop sells jackets, scarves and warm knitted tops. You buy one that you pull over your head. Which item?
On the train you take a small portable computer out of your bag and answer emails. What is it?
A student buys a light computer that she can fold and carry to university. What does she buy?
At the cafe, a freelancer works on a portable computer with a screen that folds down. What is it?
The bus is crowded and you cannot find a seat anywhere. How is the bus?
After a big dinner you cannot eat another bite. You say: 'I'm completely ...'
The glass is filled to the top with water and nothing more fits in. Which word describes it?
Your friend asks: 'Pizza or pasta?' You do not mind at all: 'It makes no difference to me.' Which word do you use?
The waiter asks if you want red or white wine, but both are fine for you. You say: 'It's all the same.'
Your boss says: 'We can meet today or tomorrow.' For you the day does not matter. Which word do you say?
In the morning you hear a small animal with wings singing on the roof. What is it?

A cat sits at the window and watches a creature with feathers on the branch outside.
The teacher gives a hard maths question and you are silent for a minute, using your brain to find the answer. What do you do?

Your friend asks a question and you say: 'Wait, let me use my head for a moment.' What do you do?

en: sports field, sports ground, playing field
situations: On Saturday the boys' football team meets at the open grass area outside town to play a match. Where do they meet?

A weather report says there is a high chance of snow tomorrow. The snow is ... to come.

en: to miss, to miss out on
situations: You run to the station but the train has already left, and you could not catch it. What happened?

At the cinema, a famous woman plays the main part in a new drama. What is her job?

Your sister studies at a drama school because she wants to appear in films one day. What will she become?
You tell your friend: 'Before the exam, I will have a coffee, but before that I must call my mum.' Which word means 'before that'?

A teacher asks: 'Who wrote this poem?' The answer is the male writer's name. What do we call him?
You wake up late and the bus leaves in five minutes. Your mother calls: 'Quick, go faster!' What must you do?
The film starts in ten minutes, and you are still at home. You tell your friend you must move quickly.
The teacher says: 'Please do not walk slowly, the class begins in one minute!' What does she want?
You look at the front of a book and read the big words at the top. What are they?

The newspaper article starts with a short, bold line at the top that tells you what it is about. What is this called?
The new flat has a smart design, clean lines and the newest technology. How would you describe it?
Your grandmother likes old things, but your sister prefers up-to-date, trendy clothes. What kind of style does she like?
An art museum shows paintings from the last few decades, not from old times. They are ... art.
You see bright flashes in the sky and hear loud bangs, and heavy rain begins. What is this weather?
Your dog hides under the bed because of the lightning and loud booms outside. What is happening?
The football match is stopped because of lightning, thunder and a heavy downpour. Why?
On the wall at the bus stop, there is a large sheet of paper advertising a concert. What is it?
For the school party, the pupils draw a big picture on paper to hang on the wall. What do they make?
You hang a big picture of your favourite band on your bedroom wall. What is it?
In the kitchen you use a knife to make small pieces of onion and tomato for the salad. What do you do?
At the barber's, the man takes scissors and makes your hair shorter. What is he doing?
You hold paper and scissors. You make the paper into two parts. What do you do?
A woman paints beautiful pictures and shows them in a gallery. What is her job?
At an art fair, a woman explains her sculptures to visitors. What do we call her?
Your aunt makes paintings and drawings and sells them at the market. What is she?
A man has no home and no money and sleeps in the street. How would you describe him?
The family cannot buy new clothes for the children because they have so little money. They are ...
In some countries, many people do not have enough to eat. These people are called ...?
Your friend says: 'You must see this film, there is no way around it!' Which word means 'without fail'?
The boss says: 'We need that report by Friday, no matter what.' Which word fits?
You tell the doctor: 'I really need an appointment today, it cannot wait.' Which word do you use?
At university you eat lunch at a big self-service room with trays and cheap food. What is it?
In the school building there is a room where pupils buy snacks and meals at lunchtime. What do we call it?
In the hospital, visitors can buy sandwiches and coffee in a simple self-service restaurant.

en: to exchange, to replace, to swap, to substitute, to share
situations: The shirt you bought is too small, so you take it back to the shop and get a bigger one. What do you do?
Two friends each have a ticket for a different day and change them with each other. What do they do?
The old battery in the remote control is dead. You put in a new one. What do you do?
After many lessons and a test, you get a small card that lets you drive a car. What is it?

You forgot your wallet, missed the bus and it started to rain. You say: 'This day is really awful.'

en: to drive away, to drive off, to leave
situations: Your parents sit in the car on Saturday morning and go on holiday, leaving the house. What do they do?

In a restaurant kitchen a man in a white hat prepares the soups and steaks. What is his job?

At the hotel, you compliment the man who made the dinner. What is his job?

en: besides, also, in addition, furthermore, moreover
situations: You say: 'I don't want to go to the party because I'm tired. Also, I have to get up early.' Which word adds a second reason?

In an email you write: 'Thank you for the offer. Besides that, I have one more question.'
You lose your wallet in the street, so you go to a man in uniform at the station to report it. Who helps you?
At the crossing a man in a blue uniform stops the cars so the children can go over. Who is he?
After a break-in at your house, a man in uniform comes to ask you some questions. Who is he?
You have a headache. The pharmacist gives you a small bottle and says it is a good thing for pain. What is it?
The government wants to fight pollution and looks for ways and tools to do it. What are these called?
A teacher says: 'Money alone is not enough. We need other resources to build the new school.'
Someone makes a mistake you think shows no clever thinking. You say: 'That was a silly idea.' How do you describe it?
A child says: 'I don't like this film, the story is boring and silly.' Which word does he use?
You lock your keys in the car and say to yourself: 'How foolish of me!'
A friend asks what to do about her problem. You tell her what you think is best. What do you do?
In a quiz, you do not know the answer, so you say a number and hope it is right. What are you doing?

A child asks where the birds and airplanes fly. You point upwards. What is that?
A man with a camera and a map stands in front of the cathedral and takes photos on his holiday. Who is he?
In summer the old town is full of men from other countries visiting the sights. Who are they?
At the museum, a man in sandals asks for a city map. He is only here for a few days on holiday.
You try on a jacket in the shop and it is exactly your size. What does the jacket do?
The key goes into the lock perfectly. It is just right. What does the key do?
Your friend says: 'Red and green do not go well together.' What do the colours not do?
A boy reads a funny paperback with pictures and speech bubbles about a superhero. What is it?
At the kiosk you buy a thin magazine with drawn pictures and short texts for children. What is it?
In a bookshop you see a shelf with illustrated stories, like those about Donald Duck.

Before the exam, your friend bites her nails and walks up and down. How is she?
You are about to go on stage in front of hundreds of people and your heart beats fast. How do you feel?

The school class takes a trip to see dinosaur bones and old tools in a big building. Where are they?
A tourist wants to see famous art. You send him to a large building with galleries. What is it?

en: to thank, to say thanks, to say thank you
situations: A neighbour looks after your cat while you are away. When you come back, you give her flowers and say 'thank you'. What do you do?

A mother tells her child: 'Carry the hot soup slowly so you don't spill it.' She wants the child to be ...

In a drugstore, there is a section with lipstick, face cream and powder. What do we call these products?

Before the party, your sister puts on lipstick and eye makeup. What products does she use?

At the crossing, the light turns red and all cars must stop. What is the device?

A box with red, yellow and green lights hangs above the crossing and tells you when to go. What is it?

en: for that reason, therefore, because of this, that's why
situations: You say: 'It was raining, and for that reason we stayed at home.' Which word connects the two ideas?

The child smiles when he sees his birthday cake. How does he feel?

A child takes crayons and makes a picture of a house and a sun. What is he doing?

en: to book, to enter, to post
situations: You go to a travel website and reserve a flight to Rome for next month. What do you do?

You open the fridge and there is no food in it at all. How is it?
The cinema is closed, and the hall has no people in it. How is it?
You look at your glass and there is nothing left in it. How is the glass?

en: on the way, en route, in transit
situations: You phone your friend: 'I'm in the car right now, I'll be there in ten minutes.' Which word means 'on the way'?
A business woman is often not at home because she travels all the time for work. She is ...

On Monday morning many cars, buses and bikes fill the roads and you move slowly. What is there a lot of?

Your uncle's son comes to visit you at Christmas. What is he to you?

Your aunt's male child is the same age as you and goes to the same school. Who is he to you?

en: to pack, to grab, to seize
situations: The day before your flight you put your clothes into the suitcase. What do you do?
For a school trip your mother helps you put sandwiches and a bottle in your bag. What are you doing?

The weightlifter can lift 200 kilos with ease. How would you describe him?

You drink a coffee that is very concentrated and makes you wide awake. The coffee is very ...

en: to photograph, to take pictures, to shoot, to take a photo
situations: On holiday, you hold your camera up and take pictures of the beautiful mountains. What do you do?

Two friends disagree: one loves the film, the other hates it. They have different ...?
In a discussion, you say clearly what you believe about the new rule. What do you give?

en: on it, to it, on that
situations: You say: 'The book is on the table and the cat is sitting on top of it.' Which word means 'on it'?
A friend asks if you are looking forward to the holiday. You say: 'Yes, I am looking forward to that.' Which word means 'to it'?
After the meal there is dessert, and for that I have been waiting all day. Which word fits?
On Sunday you and your friend go to a court and hit a yellow ball over a net with rackets. What sport is it?

The shop sells good shoes at a low price. How would you describe the offer?
You find a nice hotel room that costs very little for the quality. What is the room?
A friend asks: 'Is the restaurant expensive?' You say: 'No, it's good and costs little.' What is it?

You say to your friend at the end of an email: 'I hope you have a nice weekend!' What do you do for her?
The children laugh and run in the garden, and they have a great time. What are they having?

After the cinema you say: 'It was great, we really enjoyed ourselves.' What did you have?
At the wedding, the groom puts a small round piece of gold on the bride's finger. What is it?

You lose a small circle of silver from your finger while washing your hands. What did you lose?

You hang the wet washing in the sun, and after an hour there is no water left in it. How is it now?

The waiter asks if you want your white wine sweet or without sugar. You say: 'Not sweet, please.'

en: to renovate, to refurbish, to redecorate
situations: The walls of your flat are old and dirty, so you paint them and put in a new floor. What do you do to the flat?

You say: 'After dinner, around eight o'clock, I like to watch TV.' When do you do this regularly?

Your friend phones every day when the working day is over and it gets dark. Which word means 'in the evening'?
You take a small device out of your pocket to call your mother while walking. What is it?

After eating too many sweets, you feel a sharp pain in your mouth. Which part hurts?

You ride a roller coaster and your heart is racing. How is the ride?

Your friend returns from a trip to a jungle and tells you about all the adventures. The trip was ...
A woman in a white hat prepares the soups and desserts in the hotel kitchen. What is her job?
At a cooking school, the teacher is a woman who makes pasta in front of the class. Who is she?
You compliment the woman who made the delicious dinner in the restaurant. What is her job?
The journalist stands in front of the camera and tells the news about the fire. What does she do?

Your boss asks you to give him an update on the project at the end of the week. What should you do?
A boy breaks a plate and says he did not do it, but he did. What did he say?

You say: 'It was cold, it was even snowing.' Which word adds a surprising extra?

In the cinema, a man next to you makes this noise all the time with a sore throat. What does he do?
The doctor listens to your chest and asks if you often do this at night. What?
At the table, you cut the steak with a sharp tool with a handle. What is it?
In the kitchen the cook cuts onions with a tool with a blade. What does he use?
The table is set with a fork, a spoon and a ...
Bratwurst and beer are the kind of food you expect in Germany. How is this food?
Your friend is late again, just like always. You say: 'That is just like him.' How is it?
A tourist asks for a traditional souvenir that shows the place. What kind of gift?
You do not know what a word means in a foreign language, so you open a thick book to find it. What is it?
In the language class, the teacher tells you to bring a book with words in alphabetical order. What is it?
On your phone, you use an app to look up the meaning of a word. What kind of app is it?
The guests say goodbye and walk out of the door. What do they do?
The teacher asks: 'Can you move away from the board, please?' What do you do?
The party is boring, so you decide to go. What do you do?
On the sofa, you hold a flat touchscreen device, bigger than a phone, to read the news. What is it?
The child watches cartoons on a flat touchscreen in the car. What is it?
The waiter takes your order on a flat touchscreen instead of paper. What does he use?
At the canteen, you get a plate with a share of rice and vegetables. What do you get?
The waiter brings a plate of chips for one person. What is it?
The ice cream shop gives a child a ball of ice cream in a cup. What is it?
The lesson lasts two hours and nothing interesting happens. You nearly fall asleep. How is it?
The film has no action and no good story. How is it?
On Sunday you have nothing to do and you watch the clock. How is the day?
You ask a friend: 'Have you ever been to Paris?' Which small word means 'ever'?
Your mother says: 'Just try the soup once.' Which small word is used?
You say: 'Two times two is four.' Which word do you use for 'times'?
In Britain you speak the language of the country. Which language is it?
Your class has lessons in maths, French and the language of London. Which subject is that?
At the airport, the sign is in two languages: the local one and the language that many people in the world speak. Which?
You meet someone at a party and, after a few weeks, you cannot stop thinking about him and your heart beats fast. What do you do?
Your friend says: 'I've never felt like this, I think I'm starting to love him.' What has she done?
Romeo sees Juliet for the first time and starts to love her. What does he do?
You get tired of the city and go to the mountains, where you see trees, animals and rivers. What are you enjoying?
The school group goes outside to see plants and animals as they live. What do they see?
In the documentary, the world with mountains, lakes and animals is shown. What is the topic?
After dinner, there is a little pasta left in the pot. What is it?
You pay part of the bill now and the remaining part later. What is that part?
The teacher says: 'You may go. Others, please stay.' What do those others make up?
You write down your answers on paper in the exam instead of speaking. What kind of exam is it?
The landlord says: 'Please confirm in writing, not by phone.' How should you confirm?
The driving test has a part with questions on paper and a part on the road. How is the first part?

en: to disturb, to bother, to disrupt
situations: You study for an exam, but the neighbour plays loud music. What does the music do?
In the meeting, your phone rings and the speaker has to stop. What does your phone do?
The child enters the office while his father speaks on the phone. What does the child do?
At the zoo, you see lions, monkeys and elephants. What are they?
At home, your family has a dog, and the neighbour has a rabbit. What are they?
A child draws a horse and a cow on a farm. What are they?
After carrying a heavy bag all day, the part of your body behind your chest hurts. Which part?
The doctor looks at the part opposite your stomach. Which part?
You lie on your front, and the masseur works on the part between your neck and your hips. Which part?
You give three reasons: 'First, it is cheap. Second, it is near. ..., it is nice.' Which word starts the last one?
The teacher lists the rules: first, second, then the one that comes after second. Which word?
In your talk you give reasons: one, two, then the next one. Which word do you say?
On Sunday, your mother puts dough in the oven to make a cake. What does she do?
A baker gets up early to make rolls and bread. What does he do?
For Christmas, the children make cookies and put them in the hot oven. What do they do?
On the farm, a pink animal with a curly tail rolls in the mud. What is it?
The butcher sells chops and sausages made from an animal that says 'oink'. What animal?
Muslims and Jews do not eat meat from this animal. What is it?
On a hot day, you step into the shade and feel a nice, light cold. How is the air?
The autumn morning is a bit cold, so you take a light jacket. How is the weather?
You open the fridge, and a drink is not warm and not very cold. How is the drink?
The music is so loud that your head aches, so you put your hands over the parts on the side of your head. What are they?
The girl wears rings in the parts of her head used for hearing. What parts?
The doctor looks inside with a small light to see why you cannot hear well. What does he look at?
You put all your boxes and furniture in a van and go to a new flat. What is it called?
Friends help to carry the sofa down three flights of stairs. What are they helping with?
The family is leaving the old house, and a truck is being loaded. What is happening?

en: to pay attention, to take care, to be careful, to watch (out), to keep an eye on
situations: The teacher says: 'Listen carefully, this will be in the exam.' What does she want you to do?
Your mother asks you to watch the little baby while she goes to the shop. What do you do?
The road is icy, and your father says: 'Watch out when you walk!' What should you do?
You have a lot of work, many deadlines and no time to rest. How do you feel?
The doctor says you have headaches because of pressure at work. What is the cause?
Exam week is coming, and your tension is rising. What do you have?
At the museum, entry costs nothing for children. How is the entry?
The sign says: 'Wifi ... for guests.' What does it mean when you do not pay?
A shop gives a sample to every customer and takes no money. How is the sample?
You go to the gym on Monday and on Thursday. How many times per week?
The teacher asks you to say the word one, two times. How often?
You rang the bell, and then once more. How many times did you ring?
You fall off your bike and your knee hurts a lot. What do you feel?
The dentist asks: 'Do you feel any hurt when I touch this tooth?' What is he asking about?
The tablet helps to stop the feeling of an aching head. What does it stop?

en: to take away, to bring away, to see off
situations: A father drives his children to school and goes back home. What does he do?
After the party, you take the old chairs to the garage. What do you do?
The mechanic takes the broken car away to the workshop. What does he do?
In the kitchen, the bin is full of old packaging and food waste. What is in it?
Every Tuesday, a truck comes to collect what the residents put out in front of the houses. What do they collect?
In the park, there are bottles and papers on the ground. What is it?
On a sunny Sunday, families go to a green area with trees, grass and a pond in the city. Where?
Children play on the swings in a large green space in the city. Where are they?
You walk the dog in the green area close to your house. Where do you go?
After a long illness, you cannot lift a heavy bag. How are you?
The old man has very little power in his arms. How are his arms?
The signal on your phone is poor and you cannot call. How is the signal?

en: to travel, to go away, to go on a trip
situations: Every summer, the family packs the suitcases and goes to a faraway country. What do they do?
A businessman is not in the office because he is away on a trip. What does he do?
Next week you will be away from home for a holiday. What will you do?
A child gets a bag of chocolate, gummy bears and lollipops. What does he get?
The dentist warns: 'Do not eat too many chocolates and candies.' What does she mean?
At the cinema, you buy chocolate bars and gum at the kiosk. What are they?
On Saturday morning, people sell old clothes, books and toys from tables in a car park. What is it?
You find a cheap old lamp at a market where people sell second-hand things. Where are you?
Before moving, you want to sell your old things and put up a stall. Where do you sell them?
The kids come home from school at about 1 and play until 5. At what time of the day?
The office is closed between lunch and dinner on Fridays. When?
Your grandmother has coffee and cake every day between lunch and evening. When?
In the music room, you see a guitar, a piano and a violin. What are these?
Your mother asks: 'Which one do you want to learn to play?' What does she mean?
The orchestra's players each bring something to play music with. What do they bring?
You cut the tomato with ease because the knife is very good. How is the knife?
The curry makes your mouth burn and you drink water. How is the curry?
The mustard is so strong that tears come to your eyes. How is it?

en: to make, to create, to manage
situations: You had a lot to do, but you finished everything on time. What did you do?
The artist makes a new sculpture out of stone. What does he do?
The climber reached the top of the mountain after a hard day. What did he do?
At night you see a story in your head, in which you fly over the town, but then you wake up. What is it?
A boy says: 'My big wish is to become a pilot.' What does he have?
You tell your friend about the strange pictures that came to you while you were asleep. What do you tell?
